notes: Rubric total 20 -> hard bucket, matching task.toml 'hard' and >= the max competency floor (hard, from the formal-proofs competency C-047ea557). The task is a staged toolchain build-out (dependent_stages=3): a clean-room C compiler (zcc, authored for the task, at /app/cc-src) is installed as /app/vendor/bin/cc, /app/sections.txt is derived by compiling a probe with that very compiler and dumping its ELF sections and symbol tables with readelf, the Coq proof module is completed and compiled to a .vo proof object, the Scala 2.11 project is packaged into a standalone assembly JAR (bundle scala-library so java -jar works), and a symbolic execution engine with the z3 constraint solver is implemented and installed on PATH. tool_breadth=3 covers the compiler install/build pipeline (python front-end + as/ld via binutils), coqc, scalac+jar, readelf, z3, and the LLVM-16 toolchain. reasoning_depth=3: completing the formal proofs requires real tactic work (induction; the gauss identity needs polynomial arithmetic that plain lia cannot close, forcing nia/ring), and writing a correct symbolic executor over an IR with ITE path conditions. hidden_case_generalization=3: the engine is re-run byte-for-byte on hidden IRs (including a NO_SOLUTION case), the compiler is re-run on hidden C programs, and sections.txt is byte-compared to a rebuilt readelf dump. debugging_ambiguity=2 from compiler/codegen and proof tactic failures; adversarial_inputs=1 (the NO_SOLUTION engine case and scala arg variants); resource_pressure=2 from the multi-toolchain install/build budget and 1-cpu build. quantitative_correctness=2 for exact numeric outputs (solver models, jar arithmetic, compiled program stdout).
